subject: Physics
question: Convert a room temperature of $37^\circ\text{C}$ (human body temperature) into the absolute Kelvin scale:
explanation: $T(\text{K}) = \theta(^\circ\text{C}) + 273 = 37 + 273 = 310\text{ K}$.

subject: Physics
question: How much heat energy ($Q$) is required to raise the temperature of $3\text{ kg}$ of water from $25^\circ\text{C}$ to $45^\circ\text{C}$ (given specific heat of water $c = 4200\text{ J/(kg}\cdot\text{K)}$)?
explanation: $Q = mc\Delta T = 3\text{ kg} \times 4200\text{ J/(kg}\cdot\text{K)} \times (45 - 25)\text{ K} = 3 \times 4200 \times 20 = 252,000\text{ J} = 252\text{ kJ}$.

subject: Physics
question: A block of copper has a mass of $890\text{ g}$ and a volume of $100\text{ cm}^3$. What is its density in SI units ($\text{kg/m}^3$)?
explanation: $\rho = \frac{m}{V} = \frac{890\text{ g}}{100\text{ cm}^3} = 8.9\text{ g/cm}^3 = 8.9 \times 1000 = 8900\text{ kg/m}^3$.

subject: Physics
question: Due to anomalous expansion, water contracts on heating from $0^\circ\text{C}$ to $4^\circ\text{C}$. At what temperature is the density of water at its maximum ($1000\text{ kg/m}^3$)?
explanation: Water reaches minimum volume and maximum density at $4^\circ\text{C}$, enabling aquatic organisms to survive beneath frozen lake ice.

subject: Physics
question: How much heat energy is required to melt $0.5\text{ kg}$ of ice at $0^\circ\text{C}$ into water at $0^\circ\text{C}$ without change in temperature ($L_f = 3.36 \times 10^5\text{ J/kg}$)?
explanation: $Q = m L_f = 0.5\text{ kg} \times 3.36 \times 10^5\text{ J/kg} = 168,000\text{ J} = 168\text{ kJ}$.

subject: Physics
question: Water is widely utilized as an effective coolant in automobile car engines because of its exceptionally:
explanation: Water absorbs substantial amounts of heat with only a modest rise in temperature due to its high specific heat capacity.

subject: Physics
question: An aluminum rod of initial length $2\text{ m}$ is heated so its temperature increases by $50^\circ\text{C}$. If the coefficient of linear expansion $\alpha = 2.4 \times 10^{-5}\text{ K}^{-1}$, what is the increase in length $\Delta L$?
explanation: $\Delta L = L_0 \alpha \Delta T = 2 \times (2.4 \times 10^{-5}) \times 50 = 240 \times 10^{-5} = 2.4 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m} = 2.4\text{ mm}$.

subject: Physics
question: Mercury is preferred over water as a thermometric liquid in laboratory thermometers because mercury:

options.A: Does not wet glass, is opaque with a uniform coefficient of thermal expansion, and has a wide liquid range
options.B: Has a higher specific heat capacity than water

explanation: Mercury expands uniformly, does not wet glass walls, has a high boiling point ($357^\circ\text{C}$), and is easily visible.

subject: Physics
question: At what temperature do the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales indicate the exact same numerical value?
explanation: Setting $C = F = x \implies x = \frac{9}{5}x + 32 \implies -\frac{4}{5}x = 32 \implies x = -40^\circ$ (where $-40^\circ\text{C} = -40^\circ\text{F}$).

subject: Physics
question: For an isotropic solid material, the relationship between its coefficient of volume expansion ($\beta$) and coefficient of linear expansion ($\alpha$) is:
explanation: Volume expansion occurs in three dimensions: $\beta \approx 3\alpha$.

subject: Physics
question: How much thermal energy is needed to convert $0.2\text{ kg}$ of boiling water at $100^\circ\text{C}$ into steam at $100^\circ\text{C}$ (given $L_v = 2.26 \times 10^6\text{ J/kg}$)?
explanation: $Q = m L_v = 0.2\text{ kg} \times 2.26 \times 10^6\text{ J/kg} = 452,000\text{ J} = 452\text{ kJ}$.

subject: Physics
question: The lowest possible theoretical temperature, known as Absolute Zero ($0\text{ K}$ or $-273.15^\circ\text{C}$), is the temperature at which:

options.A: All molecular translational kinetic motion of matter ceases and gas pressure theoretically becomes zero
options.B: Water freezes into ice at sea level

explanation: Absolute zero ($0\text{ K} = -273.15^\circ\text{C}$) is the thermodynamic limit where internal kinetic energy and molecular motion reach their theoretical minimum.

subject: Physics
question: A bimetallic strip consists of brass (higher expansion coefficient) and iron (lower expansion coefficient) welded together. When heated, the strip:

options.A: Bends into a curve with the brass on the outer convex side
options.B: Bends with the iron on the outer convex side

explanation: Because brass expands more than iron for the same temperature rise, it forces the strip to bend into an arc with brass on the longer outer convex curve.

subject: Physics
question: Land breezes and sea breezes near coastal regions are caused primarily by:

options.A: Convection currents created because land has a much lower specific heat capacity than sea water and heats/cools faster
options.C: Tidal gravitational forces of the Moon

explanation: Land heats up faster than water by day, creating rising warm air and incoming sea breezes; by night, land cools faster, driving land breezes seaward.

subject: Physics
question: Two bodies placed in thermal contact are said to be in Thermal Equilibrium when:

options.A: Both bodies reach the exact same temperature and net heat transfer between them is zero
options.B: Both bodies contain identical total thermal heat energy
options.C: Both bodies have identical mass and volume

explanation: Thermal equilibrium occurs when temperatures equalize, so that the net rate of heat transfer between interacting objects is zero.

subject: Physics
question: Small gaps are intentionally left between adjacent lengths of steel railway tracks during construction in order to:

options.A: Allow space for linear thermal expansion of steel in hot summer seasons to prevent buckling
options.B: Let rainwater drain away from the rails
options.C: Reduce the weight of the railway track
options.D: Increase the speed of the train

explanation: Steel expands significantly with summer heat ($\Delta L = L_0 \alpha \Delta T$). Expansion gaps accommodate this length increase without track distortion or buckling.

subject: Physics
question: A patient's fever temperature is measured as $104^\circ\text{F}$. What is this temperature in the Celsius scale?

subject: Physics
question: A solid gold ornament has a mass of $386\text{ g}$. If the density of pure gold is $19.3\text{ g/cm}^3$, what is the volume of the ornament?
explanation: $V = \frac{m}{\rho} = \frac{386\text{ g}}{19.3\text{ g/cm}^3} = 20\text{ cm}^3$.

subject: Physics
question: The SI unit of specific heat capacity ($c = \frac{Q}{m \Delta T}$) is:
explanation: Specific heat capacity is energy per unit mass per unit temperature change, giving units of $\text{Joules per kilogram per Kelvin} = \text{J/(kg}\cdot\text{K)}$.

subject: Physics
question: Why does sweating or water evaporation produce a cooling sensation on the skin?

options.A: High-energy water molecules escape into vapor, carrying away latent heat of vaporization from the skin
options.B: Water cools the air by condensing
options.C: Water reacts chemically with skin proteins
options.D: Atmospheric pressure increases on wet surfaces

explanation: Fast-moving molecules with higher kinetic energy escape during evaporation, reducing the average kinetic energy (and temperature) of remaining liquid on the skin.

subject: Physics
question: Specific Latent Heat of Fusion ($L_f$) is defined as the heat energy required to change unit mass of a substance from solid to liquid without a change in temperature. Its SI unit is:
explanation: $L_f = \frac{Q_f}{m}$. Since heat is measured in Joules and mass in kilograms, its SI unit is $\text{J/kg}$.

subject: Physics
question: Pure water reaches its maximum density of $1000\text{ kg/m}^3$ at a temperature of:
explanation: Due to anomalous expansion, water contracts when heated from $0^\circ\text{C}$ to $4^\circ\text{C}$, reaching its minimum volume and maximum density at $4^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Physics
question: A clinical thermometer features a narrow constriction in the glass capillary tube just above the bulb in order to:

options.A: Prevent the mercury thread from falling back into the bulb before reading
options.B: Increase the boiling point of mercury
options.D: Allow the mercury to evaporate easily

explanation: The constriction allows expanding mercury to pass when heated, but when removed from the patient's body, the mercury breaks at the constriction, preserving the reading.

subject: Physics
question: The exact formula used to convert a temperature from the Celsius scale ($C$) to the Fahrenheit scale ($F$) is:
explanation: The conversion formula is $F = \frac{9}{5}C + 32 = 1.8C + 32$.

subject: Physics
question: On the standard Celsius scale, the lower fixed point ($0^\circ\text{C}$) and upper fixed point ($100^\circ\text{C}$) are defined respectively by the:

options.A: Melting point of pure ice and boiling point of pure water at standard atmospheric pressure
options.B: Freezing point of mercury and boiling point of alcohol
options.C: Absolute zero and human body temperature
options.D: Triple point of nitrogen and boiling point of water

explanation: The Celsius scale is fixed between the melting point of pure ice ($0^\circ\text{C}$) and the boiling point of pure water ($100^\circ\text{C}$) at $1\text{ atm}$.

subject: Physics
question: The change in volume ($\Delta V$) of a solid or liquid of initial volume $V_0$ when heated through temperature change $\Delta T$ is given by the formula:
explanation: Volumetric thermal expansion is given by $\Delta V = \beta V_0 \Delta T$, where $\beta$ is the coefficient of volume expansion (and $\beta = 3\alpha$).

subject: Physics
question: The phase transformation in which a solid changes directly into gas without transitioning through an intermediate liquid state is called:
explanation: Sublimation is the direct transition of a substance from solid phase to vapor phase (e.g., dry ice, camphor, iodine).

subject: Physics
question: How much heat energy ($Q$) is needed to raise the temperature of a $0.5\text{ kg}$ iron block from $20^\circ\text{C}$ to $60^\circ\text{C}$? (Specific heat of iron $c = 450\text{ J}\cdot\text{kg}^{-1}\cdot\text{K}^{-1}$):
explanation: $Q = mc\Delta T = 0.5\text{ kg} \times 450\text{ J}\cdot\text{kg}^{-1}\cdot\text{K}^{-1} \times (60 - 20)^\circ\text{C} = 0.5 \times 450 \times 40 = 9000\text{ J}$.

subject: Physics
question: Alcohol is preferred over mercury in thermometers designed for meteorological stations in polar arctic regions because:

options.A: Alcohol has a much lower freezing point ($-114^\circ\text{C}$) than mercury ($-39^\circ\text{C}$)
options.B: Alcohol has a higher boiling point than mercury
options.C: Alcohol does not expand when heated

explanation: Mercury freezes at $-39^\circ\text{C}$, rendering it useless in severe arctic climates, whereas alcohol remains liquid down to $-114^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Physics
question: Equal volumes ($100\text{ cm}^3$ each) of two miscible liquids with densities $0.8\text{ g/cm}^3$ and $1.2\text{ g/cm}^3$ are mixed thoroughly. The density of the mixture is:
explanation: Mass $m_1 = 0.8 \times 100 = 80\text{ g}$, $m_2 = 1.2 \times 100 = 120\text{ g}$. Total volume = $200\text{ cm}^3$. Density = $\frac{80 + 120}{200} = \frac{200}{200} = 1.0\text{ g/cm}^3$.

subject: Physics
question: Absolute zero ($0\text{ K}$ on the Kelvin thermodynamic temperature scale) corresponds on the Celsius scale to:
explanation: Kelvin temperature is related to Celsius by $T(\text{K}) = T(^\circ\text{C}) + 273.15$. Setting $T(\text{K}) = 0$ gives $T(^\circ\text{C}) = -273.15^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Physics
question: A section of steel railway track has an initial length of $100\text{ m}$. When the ambient temperature rises by $20^\circ\text{C}$ (coefficient of linear expansion $\alpha = 1.1 \times 10^{-5}\text{ K}^{-1}$), the thermal linear expansion $\Delta L$ is:
explanation: By the linear expansion formula: $\Delta L = \alpha L_0 \Delta T = (1.1 \times 10^{-5}\text{ K}^{-1})(100\text{ m})(20\text{ K}) = 0.022\text{ m} = 2.2\text{ cm}$.

subject: Physics
question: A bimetallic strip used in thermostats and fire alarms bends when heated because:

options.A: The two bonded metals have different coefficients of linear thermal expansion
options.B: One metal becomes magnetic while the other remains non-magnetic
options.C: One metal melts while the other freezes
options.D: Thermal insulation cools the inner strip surface

explanation: A bimetallic strip consists of two dissimilar metal strips (e.g. brass and iron) welded together. Because brass expands more than iron for the same temperature rise, the strip bends into an arc towards the metal with lower expansion.

subject: Physics
question: The specific latent heat of vaporization of water ($L_v \approx 2.26 \times 10^6\text{ J/kg}$) is the thermal energy required to:

options.A: Change $1\text{ kg}$ of boiling water into steam at its boiling point ($100^\circ\text{C}$) without any change in temperature
options.B: Raise the temperature of $1\text{ kg}$ of water by $1^\circ\text{C}$
options.C: Melt $1\text{ kg}$ of solid ice into water at $0^\circ\text{C}$
options.D: Cool $1\text{ kg}$ of steam to liquid water at room temperature

explanation: Specific latent heat of vaporization ($L_v$) is defined as the quantity of heat energy required to change unit mass ($1\text{ kg}$) of a liquid into gas at its boiling point without any change in temperature.

subject: Physics
question: Due to the anomalous thermal expansion of water, when water is cooled from $4^\circ\text{C}$ down to $0^\circ\text{C}$, its volume:
explanation: Unlike typical liquids, water expands when cooled from $4^\circ\text{C}$ to $0^\circ\text{C}$ (anomalous expansion), causing ice and cold water below $4^\circ\text{C}$ to be less dense and float on top of lakes.

subject: Physics
question: A clinical mercury-in-glass thermometer is engineered with a sharp capillary constriction (kink) just above the bulb primarily in order to:

options.A: Prevent the thermometric mercury column from contracting back into the bulb before the reading can be noted
options.B: Accelerate the heating of mercury in the bulb
options.C: Allow the thermometer to withstand boiling water

explanation: The narrow constriction prevents the mercury thread from falling back when the thermometer is removed from the patient’s body, allowing accurate reading of maximum body temperature until shaken down.

subject: Physics
question: The heat capacity ($C$) of an entire physical body of mass $m$ and specific heat capacity $c$ is given by the formula:
explanation: Heat capacity is the thermal energy needed to raise the temperature of the entire body by $1\text{ K}$ (or $1^\circ\text{C}$), defined as $C = \frac{Q}{\Delta T} = mc$, with SI unit $\text{J/K}$.

subject: Physics
question: Which of the following environmental factors will INCREASE the rate of evaporation of a liquid from an open container?

options.A: Increasing the exposed liquid surface area and increasing temperature
options.D: Covering the container with an airtight lid

explanation: Evaporation rate increases with larger surface area, higher liquid temperature, higher wind speed over the surface, and lower ambient humidity.

subject: Physics
question: A solid copper sample has a measured density of $8.9\text{ g/cm}^3$. Expressed in standard SI units ($\text{kg/m}^3$), its density is:
explanation: Since $1\text{ g/cm}^3 = \frac{10^{-3}\text{ kg}}{10^{-6}\text{ m}^3} = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3$, multiplying $8.9\text{ g/cm}^3 \times 1000 = 8900\text{ kg/m}^3$.

subject: Physics
question: A thermocouple thermometer measures rapid temperature changes based on what thermometric property?

options.A: The thermoelectric electromotive force (voltage) produced across two junctions of dissimilar metals kept at different temperatures (Seebeck effect)
options.B: The volumetric expansion of liquid mercury in a glass bore
options.C: The change in electrical resistance of a copper wire
options.D: The pressure variation of an ideal gas at constant volume

explanation: A thermocouple consists of two dissimilar metallic wires joined at two junctions; when the junctions are at different temperatures, a temperature-dependent voltage (thermoelectric EMF) is generated (Seebeck effect).

subject: Physics
question: At what temperature do the Celsius and Fahrenheit temperature scales display the exact same numerical reading?
explanation: Setting $F = C$: $C = \frac{9}{5}C + 32 \implies C - \frac{9}{5}C = 32 \implies -\frac{4}{5}C = 32 \implies C = -40^\circ$. Thus, $-40^\circ\text{C} = -40^\circ\text{F}$.

subject: Physics
question: Which thermometric property is utilized in a standard liquid-in-glass laboratory thermometer?

options.A: Uniform thermal expansion of liquid volume with changing temperature
options.B: Variation of electrical resistance with temperature
options.C: Change in gas pressure at fixed volume
options.D: Thermal electromotive force generated at a thermocouple junction

explanation: A liquid-in-glass thermometer (containing mercury or alcohol) operates on the principle that the liquid column volume expands linearly and uniformly with an increase in temperature.

subject: Physics
question: How much thermal energy is needed to completely melt $0.5\text{ kg}$ of ice at $0^\circ\text{C}$ into water at $0^\circ\text{C}$ ($L_f = 3.36 \times 10^5\text{ J/kg}$)?
explanation: $Q = m L_f = 0.5\text{ kg} \times 3.36 \times 10^5\text{ J/kg} = 1.68 \times 10^5\text{ J} = 168\text{ kJ}$.

subject: Physics
question: A bimetallic strip made of brass (larger coefficient $\alpha$) and iron (smaller coefficient $\alpha$) is heated uniformly. The strip bends such that:

options.A: Brass forms the outer convex curve and iron forms the inner concave curve
options.B: Iron forms the outer convex curve and brass forms the inner concave curve
options.C: The strip remains straight but increases in thickness
options.D: The strip twists spirally along its longitudinal axis

explanation: Since brass has a higher coefficient of linear expansion than iron, it expands more for the same temperature increase, forming the longer outer convex side while iron forms the inner concave side.

subject: Physics
question: A $100\text{ m}$ long copper pipe expands when its temperature rises by $50^\circ\text{C}$. If $\alpha = 1.7 \times 10^{-5}\text{ K}^{-1}$, what is the increase in length $\Delta L$?
explanation: $\Delta L = \alpha L_0 \Delta T = 1.7 \times 10^{-5} \times 100\text{ m} \times 50 = 0.085\text{ m} = 8.5\text{ cm}$.

subject: Physics
question: Why does human perspiration cool the body less effectively on a humid, muggy day?

options.A: High atmospheric humidity reduces the rate of water evaporation from the skin
options.B: Sweat contains fewer electrolytes on humid days
options.C: Humid air absorbs heat directly into the skin
options.D: The body stops sweating completely in high humidity

explanation: Evaporation is a cooling process because escaping high-energy molecules carry away latent heat. When surrounding air is already saturated with water vapor (high humidity), the net evaporation rate drops drastically.

subject: Physics
question: Water is widely utilized as an effective industrial and automotive coolant because of its remarkably high:
explanation: Water has an unusually high specific heat capacity ($4200\text{ J}/(\text{kg}\cdot\text{K})$), meaning it can absorb massive amounts of heat energy with only a modest rise in temperature.

subject: Physics
question: Why is water widely utilized as the circulating coolant in automobile engine radiators?

options.A: It possesses an exceptionally high specific heat capacity ($c = 4200\text{ J}/(\text{kg}\cdot^\circ\text{C})$)
options.B: It has very low thermal expansion compared to other liquids
options.C: It freezes easily at low winter temperatures
options.D: It exhibits high electrical conductivity under pressure

explanation: Because of its unusually high specific heat capacity ($4200\text{ J}/(\text{kg}\cdot^\circ\text{C})$), water can absorb a tremendous amount of thermal energy from the running engine with only a moderate rise in temperature.

subject: Physics
question: How is the rate of surface evaporation of a liquid affected by high atmospheric humidity?

options.A: Evaporation decreases because the surrounding air is already near saturation with moisture
options.B: Evaporation increases because moist air absorbs more latent heat
options.C: Evaporation remains completely unchanged by humidity levels
options.D: Evaporation stops instantly and turns into boiling

explanation: When humidity is high, the surrounding air holds a high concentration of water vapor molecules, which reduces the net rate of escape of energetic liquid molecules into the vapor phase.

subject: Physics
question: Why are small deliberate gaps left between consecutive steel rail tracks on railway lines?

options.A: To allow free linear thermal expansion in hot summer weather and prevent track buckling
options.B: To increase the speed of moving trains
options.C: To save manufacturing material during track laying
options.D: To allow rainwater drainage from the track bed

explanation: Steel expands in hot summer weather. Expansion gaps accommodate this thermal elongation without building destructive compressive stresses that would buckle the tracks.
